title: Canonical mutation reconciliation performance scenario
description: The ordered workload proves the authored semantic outcome and performance declaration.

injection.target: accepted or rejected outcome local-base reconciliation

parameters.scenario: return an authoritative row and server_version with a terminal mutation outcome
parameters.defect: retain the pre-outcome local base or version while marking the mutation terminal

parameters.scenario: issue update and delete concurrently from the same current base version
parameters.defect: allow both to apply, omit the loser conflict outcome, or discard the winning transition

injection.target: conflict comparison and accepted version allocation

parameters.scenario: submit equal, past, and future client_version values against the same base state
parameters.defect: let client time change winner, server version, source updated_at, or write order

parameters.scenario: submit create, upsert, and resurrection-shaped operations for an existing row
parameters.defect: accept an operation outside push insert/update/delete instead of rejecting it

parameters.scenario: create, update, and delete a registered row through local SQLite
parameters.defect: reject local CRUD unless the application calls a separate upload API

parameters.scenario: push create, update, and delete mutations for each registered table
parameters.defect: delegate one CRUD operation to an application-specific transport instead of the canonical Synchro mutation contract

parameters.scenario: apply a pull, rebuild, seed, or push-response row to local SQLite
parameters.defect: leave CDC enabled so the authoritative apply is enqueued as new client intent

parameters.scenario: accept an update whose client_version and updated_at are both controlled
parameters.defect: reuse the prior version or derive the new version from client data rather than the server fence

parameters.scenario: remove a row solely because its last local scope provenance was pruned
parameters.defect: create a delete mutation or tombstone without a server-supplied authoritative tombstone

injection.target: scope data apply and cursor transaction

parameters.scenario: kill the client at the commit boundary for an incremental page
parameters.defect: persist the new cursor without all data or all data without its paired cursor decision

injection.target: native client server-decision and local-durability boundary

parameters.scenario: deliver server assignment, schema, conflict, cursor, and rebuild decisions to the native client
parameters.defect: override a server decision or delegate local SQLite queue and safe apply to JavaScript

parameters.scenario: synchronize local SQL create, update, and delete against a registered table
parameters.defect: require an application-defined upload endpoint before canonical push can execute

steps.description: Materialize the accepted mutation before the pull closes the pending cycle.

assertions.description: The ordered workload produces the complete authored durable semantic outcome without partial state.
Every declared budget or measurement records all configured strata and required metrics.
The concurrent update-delete control detects two accepted transitions or a missing authoritative loser outcome.
The client-time control detects any authoritative outcome that changes only because client_version changes.
The operation-vocabulary control detects an accepted noncanonical push operation or implicit resurrection.
Direct native SQLite inspection proves application CRUD uses the registered table without an upload API.
The registered-table insert, update, and delete outcomes remain canonical across native and server observations.
Authoritative pull application leaves no new pending or rejected client-originated mutation.
The accepted transition installs a nonempty server version that differs from client-authored time data.
Native cleanup inspection rejects any local delete intent that lacks an authoritative tombstone.
The pulled row and its per-scope cursor become durable together and remain paired after native inspection.
The native client owns SQLite queue and safe apply while retaining server-issued outcomes and cursor decisions.
Local SQLite and canonical Synchro requests complete registered CRUD without an application upload endpoint.
